From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-qq]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-qq]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}

From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-qq]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-qq]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}

Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Tumulus, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Tumulus |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal burial mound said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-qq]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq---qq]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-qq]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳}}

|title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Tumulus, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Tumulus |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-qq]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-qq]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}

(UTC)}} [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Tumulus, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Tumulus |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal burial mound said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-->[[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq-Octagonal Kofun-->[[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳}}

(UTC)}} [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Tumulus, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Tumulus |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal burial mound said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated start]][[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated start]][[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳}}

Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal burial mound said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:Tier 2]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated start]][[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]][[Category:Tier 2]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated start]][[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}

(UTC)}} [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Tumulus, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Tumulus |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal burial mound said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated start]][[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated start]][[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳}}

(UTC)}} [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Tumulus, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Tumulus |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal burial mound said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:qq deprecated close]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}

(UTC)}} [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Tumulus, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Tumulus |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal burial mound said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳}}

From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Unsorted]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}

From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} [[Category:Ugoodbye $1]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] [[Category:Ugoodbye $1]][[Category:Completion tier 1]] [[Category:qq]][[sn:Octagonal Kofun]][[Category:qq]] [[Category:tier 2]][[Category:tier 1]][[Category: Completion categories]] [[Category:Octagonal Kofun]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Octagonal Kofun}}[[ja:八角墳]] ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024年5月 |脚注の不足=2024年5月 |独自研究=2024年5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|天武天皇}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Tumulus Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}
