{{afc comment|1=see [[every:Octagonal Kofun]] for the history[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 02:25, 31 March 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=Page originally made on english wikipedia in draftspace. g13 deleted and archived on everybodywiki. Go to [[:en:Wikipedia:Requests for undeletion]] to request undeletion of original page [[:en:draft:Octagonal Kofun]] and import the revisions to here for attribution. View on everybodywiki here [[:every:Octagonal Kofun|Octagonal Kofun]]. [[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 21:01, 16 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{afc comment|1=This page was originally created by Immanuelle as a wikipedia draft. It was then automatically transferred to everybodywiki and recovered from there. In the future it will be good to import the revisions. Check page history in case this page was moved, since the everybodywiki page may have been under a different title[[User:Immanuelle|Immanuelle]] ([[User talk:Immanuelle|talk]]) 20:10, 11 February 2025 (UTC)}} {{draft}} [[Category:Completion tier 7]] [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳}}

[[ファイル:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|発掘中の八角墳（[[中山荘園古墳]]）]] [[ファイル:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|復元整備された八角墳（[[牽牛子塚古墳]]）]]
'''八角墳'''（はっかくふん）は[[古墳時代]]の終末期（[[7世紀]]半ば）に造られた正[[八角形]]の[[古墳]]。[[京都市]]の[[御廟野古墳]]（現・[[天智天皇]]陵）や[[奈良県]][[高市郡]][[明日香村]]の[[野口王墓|野口王墓古墳]]（現・[[天武天皇|天武]]・[[持統天皇|持統]]合葬陵）などが有名。
== 八角墳の意味 == 八角墳の意味については、[[道教]]を含めた広い意味での[[古代]][[中国]]の政治思想において、[[八角形]]が天下八方の支配者にふさわしいという思想の影響が考えられる。
'''八角墳'''は[[森浩一]]の提唱によると最終末古墳に含まれる。即位した[[大王 (ヤマト王権)|大王]]が祭られている可能性を指摘する学者もあるが、奈良県だけではなく[[東京都]][[多摩市]]の[[稲荷塚古墳]]をはじめ[[東日本]]など各地で少数ではあるが確認されていることから、即位した大王だけを祭るために造られている可能性に疑いを持つ学者も多い<ref>[[宮内庁書陵部]]など（朝日新聞 2010年9月10日）</ref>。
八角墳は7世紀の半ばになると、大王墓のみが営むようになる。現在知られている限りでは、[[奈良県]][[桜井市]]の[[段ノ塚古墳]]（現[[舒明天皇]]陵）、奈良県[[高市郡]][[明日香村]]の[[野口王墓]]（現天武・持統陵）、一般に[[文武天皇]]陵と考えられている奈良県明日香村[[中尾山古墳]]<ref group="注" name="nakao">[[1974年]]（[[昭和]]49年）事前調査で八角墳であることが分かった。この古墳は[[1697年]]（[[元禄]]10年）の奈良奉行与力の見聞録に「塚形丸く根回り三十五間あり、頂上東の方へ掘り崩した跡のように窪みがあり、その中に四尺に三尺の石がある」と記録されている。</ref><ref name="nakao">[[#河上|河上(2005) 64ページ]]。</ref>、それに[[御廟野古墳]]などが八角形平面の墳丘を持っている。7世紀半ば、日本では初めて大王に固有の型式の陵墓が出現したといえる。これらのほかに、奈良県高市郡[[高取町]]の[[束明神古墳]]（[[草壁皇子]]の真弓山稜か）、方形墳の上に八角形の墳丘を造っている可能性のある明日香村の[[岩屋山古墳]]（[[斉明天皇]]陵か）などが八角形墳の可能性を指摘されている。<ref>『知識ゼロからの古墳入門』74-75頁 広瀬 和雄 （監修） </ref>
八角墳は、[[舒明天皇]]の墓から始まっていると考えられ、日本の[[大王 (ヤマト王権)|大王]]の墓に固有の型式の[[陵墓]]が考え出されたと捉えることができる。これは、大王を他の有力豪族からも隔絶した支配者とみなし、[[中央集権国家]]の樹立を目指すものであったと考えられる。
=== 墳形の変化 === この墳形の被葬者は、既述のように天皇やその近親者と考えられるので、八角形墳は、天皇の固有の型式として使用され始めたと言える。上八角下方墳の舒明陵が最も古いと仮定するなら、もとは方墳を基礎に構築されたと推定できるので、6世紀末以降の天皇陵は前方後円墳 → （大型円墳） → 大型方墳 → 上八角下方墳 → 八角墳と変化したと考えられる<ref name="kawakami">[[#河上|河上(2005) 71ページ]]。</ref>。
== 最近の調査結果 == [[2006年]]（[[平成]]18年）[[4月19日]]、[[大阪府]][[茨木市]]の[[桑原遺跡]]の桑原古墳群で[[7世紀]]の埋没群集墳24基を検出した中の1基が'''八角墳'''であり、[[藤原鎌足|中臣鎌足]]の墓の可能性を指摘する声があり、[[マスメディア]]でも紹介された。
また、[[2009年]]から[[2010年]]にかけて奈良県明日香村の[[牽牛子塚古墳]]の調査が明日香村教育委員会によっておこなわれ、2010年9月、調査成果が公表された。
== 主な古墳 == ;大王陵 *[[段ノ塚古墳]]（現・[[舒明天皇]]陵） - 奈良県桜井市 *[[御廟野古墳]]（現・[[天智天皇]]陵） - 京都市 *[[野口王墓|野口王墓古墳]]（現・[[天武天皇|天武]]・[[持統天皇|持統]]合葬陵） - 奈良県高市郡明日香村・[[7世紀]]後半（上八角下方墳） *[[中尾山古墳]]（[[文武天皇]]陵の可能性高い） - 奈良県明日香村・8世紀初頭 *[[束明神古墳]]（草壁皇子の真弓山稜の蓋然性が高く、八角墳の可能性がある。奈良県高市郡[[高取町]]） *[[岩屋山古墳]]（斉明陵の可能性。方形墳の上に八角形の墳丘を営んでいた可能性が強い。 *[[牽牛子塚古墳]]（斉明陵の可能性<ref>[http://www.asukamura.jp/chosa_hokoku/kengoshizuka/kengoshizuka.html 牽牛子塚古墳]（明日香村公式ホームページ）</ref>）奈良県明日香村越、2010年9月斉明陵の可能性強まるとの報道<ref name="毎日">{{cite news |title=牽牛子塚古墳：斉明天皇陵と特定 八角構造が判明／奈良 |newspaper=毎日新聞 |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}</ref><ref name="時事">{{cite news |title=墳丘は八角形、「斉明陵」強まる＝牽牛子塚古墳、発掘で確認―奈良・明日香村 |newspaper=時事通信社 |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}}</ref>
;首長墓 *[[稲荷塚古墳]]：[[東京都]][[多摩市]]百草・[[7世紀]]前半<ref group="注" name="inari">周濠のなかに墳丘の隅角の陵が見える程度で、外護列石などがなく、不安定な八角形で八角円墳では。基本的には[[円墳]]ではないかと推測される。直径18メートル。</ref><ref name="inari">[[#河上|河上(2005) 67 ページ]]。</ref> *[[三津屋古墳]]：[[群馬県]][[北群馬郡]][[吉岡町]]・[[7世紀]]前半 *[[経塚古墳]]：[[山梨県]][[笛吹市]]（旧[[一宮町 (山梨県)|一宮町]]）・1994年発見・[[7世紀]]前半 *[[伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|伊勢塚古墳]]：[[群馬県]][[藤岡市]]・[[6世紀]]前半 *[[中山荘園古墳]]：[[兵庫県]][[宝塚市]]<ref group="注" name="nakayama">墳丘裾の外護列石が八角形をしている。対角長の長さ13メートル。幅8.2メートル、奥行き4.2メートルの方形土壇が付いている。確実に八角形かどうかはなお検討の余地がある。</ref><ref name="nakayama">[[#河上|河上(2005) 66ページ]]。</ref>
;八角墳である可能性が指摘されている古墳 *[[尾市1号墳]] - [[広島県]][[福山市]][[新市町]]<ref group="注" name="osi">墳丘裾に列石があり、前面は直線であるが、後背面が曲線であるので、多少疑問が残る。</ref><ref name="osi">[[#河上|河上(2005) 66ページ]]。</ref> *[[神保一本杉古墳]] - [[群馬県]][[高崎市]][[吉井町 (群馬県)|吉井町]]<ref group="注" name="jinnbo">二段築造、下段は長辺が9メートル、短辺が約6.3メートルの八角形墳で、上段の墳丘は円形である。対角長東西18.5メートル、南北21メートルで長八角墳といえるかも知れない。7世紀後半の築造。</ref><ref name="jinnbo">[[#河上|河上(2005) 66ページ]]。</ref> ;八角墳である可能性が指摘されている遺構 *[[武井廃寺塔跡古墳]] - 群馬県<ref group="注" name="takei">径20メートル、一辺6.4メートルの正八角形。塔心礎とするものもその構造からは火葬の蔵骨器を入れる外容器と考えられる。時代は7世紀末から8世紀初め頃。地方における数少ない正八角形墳。</ref><ref name="takei">[[#河上|河上(2005) 67ページ]]。</ref>
== 脚注 == {{脚注ヘルプ}} === 注釈 === {{Reflist|group="注"}} === 出典 === {{Reflist|30em}}
== 参考文献 == *[[白石太一郎]]『古墳とヤマト政権』[[文藝春秋]]<[[文春新書]]>、1999年。ISBN 4-16-660036-2 *{{Cite book | 和書|author=河上邦彦|authorlink=河上邦彦 |year=2005 |title=大和の終末期古墳|publisher=[[学生社]] |isbn=978-4-311-20282-7 |ref=河上}}

Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳}}

From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|12=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|12=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|12=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|12=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|12=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|12=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|12=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|12=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|12=draft}}

(UTC)}} {{draft}} [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|12=draft|12=draft}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|12=draft|12=draft}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|12=draft|12=draft}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|12=draft|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部|12=draft|12=draft}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|12=draft|12=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|12=draft|12=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}

(UTC)}} {{draft}} [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|12=draft|12=draft}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|12=draft|12=draft}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|12=draft|12=draft}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|12=draft|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部|12=draft|12=draft}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|12=draft|12=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|12=draft|12=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡|12=draft|12=draft}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}

Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|12=draft|12=draft}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市|12=draft|12=draft}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|12=draft|12=draft}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|12=draft|12=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村|12=draft|12=draft}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|12=draft|12=draft}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市|12=draft|12=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|12=draft|12=draft}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部|12=draft|12=draft}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|12=draft|12=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|12=draft|12=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|12=draft|12=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|12=draft|12=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}

From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|12=draft|12=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|12=draft|12=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|12=draft|12=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|12=draft|12=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|12=draft|12=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|12=draft|12=draft}}

(UTC)}} {{draft}} [[File:220311_Kengoshiduka_1.jpg|thumb|{{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} a notable Octagonal Kofun, where [[Empress Kōgyoku]] is buried.]] {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

{{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

[[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

{{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}

Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[Empress Kōgyoku]] in {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ({{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}})]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenji|ja|天智天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Kyoto City|ja|京都市|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and the {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft}} and {{ill|Empress Jitō|ja|持統天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) in {{ill|Asuka, Nara|ja|明日香村|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as {{ill|Tama City|ja|多摩市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, {{ill|Tokyo|ja|東京都|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the {{ill|Imperial Household Agency Archives|ja|宮内庁書陵部|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (present-day mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Jomei|ja|舒明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in {{ill|Ibaraki City|ja|茨木市|qq=draft|qq=draft}}, Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to {{ill|Fujiwara no Kamatari|ja|藤原鎌足|qq=draft|qq=draft}}. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with {{ill|Empress Saimei|ja|斉明天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}.{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Nakaoyama Kofun|ja|中尾山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (likely mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Monmu|ja|文武天皇|qq=draft|qq=draft}}) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * {{ill|Nakayamasōen Kofun|ja|中山荘園古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}} - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft}}* {{ill|Kajiyama Kofun|ja|梶山古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
* {{ill|Kengoshizuka Kofun|ja|牽牛子塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
* {{ill|Takei temple ruins|ja|武井廃寺塔跡|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
* {{ill|Yoshida Kofun|ja|吉田古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
