Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] (likely mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Monmu|Emperor Monmu]]) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemyojin Kofun|qq=}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuya Kofun|qq=}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * [[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]] - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|qq=}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=}}* [[:en:Kajiyama Kofun|Kajiyama Kofun]]

Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}[[Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] (likely mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Monmu|Emperor Monmu]]) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemyojin Kofun|qq=}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] (likely mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Monmu|Emperor Monmu]]) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemyojin Kofun|qq=}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuya Kofun|qq=}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * [[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]] - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|qq=}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=}}* [[:en:Kajiyama Kofun|Kajiyama Kofun]]

Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] (likely mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Monmu|Emperor Monmu]]) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemyojin Kofun|qq=}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] (likely mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Monmu|Emperor Monmu]]) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemyojin Kofun|qq=}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]] in [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]]{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}[[:en:Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - {{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]] in [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]]{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}[[:en:Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] (likely mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Monmu|Emperor Monmu]]) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemyojin Kofun|qq=}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * [[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]] - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|qq=}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=}}* [[:en:Kajiyama Kofun|Kajiyama Kofun]]

{{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]] in [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]]{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}[[:en:Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] (likely mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Monmu|Emperor Monmu]]) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemyojin Kofun|qq=}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuya Kofun|qq=}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * [[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]] - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|qq=}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=}}* [[:en:Kajiyama Kofun|Kajiyama Kofun]]

{{nihongo|{{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=Octagonal Kofun|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}|八角墳|''hakkaku-fun''}} is a kind of [[Kofun]] Many Japanese Emperors were buried in them including [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Kōgyoku]] in [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]]{{Cite web |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun Kofun, Koshitsuka-gomon Kofun Kofun |url=http://asuka-japan-heritage.jp/global/en/saimei/detail/kengosiduka_sa.html |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}[[:en:Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) - Kyoto City * {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (Emperor Tenmu and Empress Jitō’s joint mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * [[:en:Nakaoyama Kofun|Nakaoyama Kofun]] (likely mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Monmu|Emperor Monmu]]) - Nara Prefecture, Asuka Village * {{ill|Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Tsukamyojin Kofun|lt=Takemyojin Kofun|ja|束明神古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Takemyojin Kofun|qq=}} (possible mausoleum of Prince Kusakabe) - Nara Prefecture, Takatori Town === Chief's Graves === * {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}} - Tokyo, Tama City (7th century) * {{ill|Mitsuya Kofun|ja|三津屋古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mitsuya Kofun|qq=}} - Gunma Prefecture, Kitagumma District * [[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]] - Hyōgo Prefecture, Takarazuka City === Others === * {{ill|Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|ja|伊勢塚古墳 (藤岡市)|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ise Kofun (Fujioka City)|qq=}} * {{ill|Oichi No.1 Kofun|ja|尾市1号墳|1=Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Oichi No.1 Kofun|qq=}}* [[:en:Kajiyama Kofun|Kajiyama Kofun]]

|website=Exploring the Footsteps of the Heroines of Asuka |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2022-03-04 |title=Octagonal Kofun said to belong to ancient Japan empress reconstructed in Nara Pref. |language=en |work=Mainichi Daily News |url=https://mainichi.jp/english/articles/20220304/p2a/00m/0na/040000c |access-date=2023-10-20}}, [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]] in {{ill|Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|lt=his Mausoleum|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mausoleum of Emperor Tenji|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}{{Cite web |title= |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33021 |access-date=2023-10-21 }}, and [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]] in {{ill|Dannozuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}[[:en:Emperor Jomei|i]]{{Cite web |last=Hays |first=Jeffrey |title=ASUKA, FUJIWARA AND ASUKA-ERA CITIES AND TOMBS {{!}} Facts and Details |url=https://factsanddetails.com/japan/cat16/sub106/entry-5299.html#chapter-16 |access-date=2023-10-20 |website=factsanddetails.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |date=2023-10-16 |title=Dan-no-tsuka Kofun [Dannotsuka Kofun 段ノ塚古墳, Jomei Tennō-ryō Jomei Tennnoryo 舒明天皇] Passage Grave : The Megalithic Portal and Megalith Map |url=https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |access-date=2023-10-20 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231016234831/https://www.megalithic.co.uk/article.php?sid=33044 |archive-date=2023-10-16 }}. From the end of the 6th century to the beginning of the 7th, the tumuli of the monarchs changed from {{ill|Square Kofun|lt=square ''hōfun'' tumuli|ja|方墳|1=Square Kofun|1=Square Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Square Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} to octagonal {{ill|Octagonal Kofun|lt=''hakkaku-fun''|ja|八角墳|1=Octagonal Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Octagonal Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} tumuli.{{sfn|Niiro|1992|p=160}} ==Overview== {{複数の問題 |出典の明記=2024th year 5月 |More footnotes needed=2024th year 5月 |独自研究=2024th year 5月 }} [[File:Nakayamashouen Kohun(digging up).jpg|thumb|Excavation of an octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Nakayamasōen Kofun|Nakayamasōen Kofun]])]] [[File:220311 Kengoshiduka 1.jpg|thumb|Restored octagonal tumulus ([[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]])]] '''Hakkakufun''' (八角墳) refers to octagonal tumuli constructed during the late [[Kofun period]] (mid-[[:en:7th century|7th century]]). Notable examples include the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Tenji|Emperor Tenji]]) in [[:en:Kyoto|Kyoto City]] and the {{ill|Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi-ōsaka Kofun|lt=Noguchi Royal Tomb|ja|野口王墓|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Noguchi Royal Tomb|qq=}} (shared mausoleum of {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|ja|Emperor Tenmu|1=Emperor Tenmu|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|13=User:Immanuelle/Emperor Tenmu|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} and [[:en:Empress Jitō|Empress Jitō]]) in [[:en:Asuka, Nara|Asuka, Nara]]. == Meaning of Hakkakufun == The significance of the octagonal shape is thought to be influenced by ancient Chinese political and philosophical ideologies, including [[Taoism]], where the octagon symbolized control over the eight cardinal directions, befitting a ruler. According to {{ill|Mori Kōichi|ja|森浩一|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mori Kōichi|qq=|1=Kōichi Mori|comment=changed title based on wikidata|WD=Q11539977}}, Hakkakufun are categorized as terminal tumuli. While some scholars believe these were exclusively imperial tombs, the presence of octagonal tumuli in locations such as [[:en:Tama, Tokyo|Tama City]], [[:en:Tokyo|Tokyo]], including the {{ill|Inarizuka Kofun|ja|稲荷塚古墳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inarizuka Kofun|qq=}}, suggests broader usage.Research by the [[:en:Archives and Mausolea Department|Imperial Household Agency Archives]], as reported in Asahi Shimbun, September 10, 2010. Hakkakufun began exclusively as imperial tombs around the mid-7th century. Examples include the {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (present-day mausoleum of [[:en:Emperor Jomei|Emperor Jomei]]) and the {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}. These signify the first appearance of a distinctive burial style unique to Japanese emperors, emphasizing centralized authority. === Evolution of Kofun Shapes === Hakkakufun are associated with emperors and their relatives, marking the emergence of a distinct imperial burial style. If the oldest example is the octagonal base of {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}}, the transition from square tumuli suggests a progression: keyhole-shaped → large round → large square → octagonal base → full octagonal tumuli.{{ill|Kawakami Kunihiko|ja|河上邦彦|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kawakami Kunihiko|qq=}}, ''Final Tumuli of Yamato,'' 2005, p. 71. == Recent Discoveries == In April 2006, an octagonal tumulus was identified among 24 clustered tumuli at the {{ill|Kuwabara Site|ja|桑原遺跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kuwabara Site|qq=|ja_comment=jawiki link invalid}} in [[:en:Ibaraki, Osaka|Ibaraki City]], Osaka Prefecture. This discovery fueled speculation that the tomb might belong to [[:en:Fujiwara no Kamatari|Fujiwara no Kamatari]]. From 2009 to 2010, investigations of the [[:en:Kengoshizuka Kofun|Kengoshizuka Kofun]] in Asuka Village were conducted, and in September 2010, it was confirmed to be octagonal, strengthening its association with [[:en:Empress Kōgyoku|Empress Saimei]].{{cite news |title=Kengoshizuka Kofun confirmed as Empress Saimei’s tomb |newspaper=Mainichi Shimbun |date=2010-09-10 |url=http://mainichi.jp/select/wadai/news/20100910k0000m040050000c.html}}{{cite news |title=Octagonal structure confirmed at Kengoshizuka Kofun, likely Empress Saimei's tomb |newspaper=Jiji Press |date=2010-09-09 |url=http://www.jiji.com/jc/c?g=soc_30&k=2010090900686}} == Prominent Tumuli == === Imperial Mausolea === * {{ill|Dannotsuka Kofun|ja|段ノ塚古墳|1=Dannozuka Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannotsuka Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Dannozuka Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Jomei's mausoleum) - Nara Prefecture, Sakurai City * {{ill|Gobyōno Kofun|ja|御廟野古墳|1=Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyōno Kofun|13=User:Immanuelle/Gobyō-no-Kofun|qq=|comment=enwiki is a redirect}} (Emperor Tenji's mausoleum) -
